title: How do you make a luxury property film with AI and no shoot day?
description: A 28-second Paradise Valley property trailer from one prompt and three reference pictures. Five of the six shots are locked off, which is what makes the single camera move land.

faq.q: How do you keep the same person, car and house across every shot of an AI video?
faq.a: Cast it with references before you prompt it. Three approved stills — subject, vehicle, property — pinned as references means every cut in a single generation agrees on who and what it is looking at. Scenery is cheap to describe in words; identity is not, so don't spend reference slots on it.

faq.q: How do you stop an AI video camera from drifting?
faq.a: Say it structurally and negatively. A spine line — 'THE CAMERA NEVER MOVES IN SHOTS 1–5' — plus an explicit NOT block banning drift, handheld shake, pans and zooms. Then verify by measuring inter-frame pixel difference rather than by watching.
